# Sterling architecture & extension document (generated)

Sterling documents and extends itself by the same registry + checked-contract +
fail-loud discipline it imposes (§15). For every extensible set below: the
registry is the single source of truth, the named checks guard it, and the
"extending this" guidance is quoted from the set's owning feature article —
the durable store is authoritative; this file is a projection of it.

## Extensible set: record-types — Record types (durable knowledge shapes)

- Registry: packages/schemas/src/records.ts — RECORD_TYPES (schema + fts + fileKeys per member) + SYSTEM_REASONS/DRAIN_VERBS
- Checks: schemas registry test (1:1, unregistered rejected) + store write validation on every create

**Extending this:** To add a record type: (1) define its zod schema in records.ts and nowhere else (invariant 1); (2) add one RECORD_TYPES entry with schema, immutable, fts, fileKeys and digest — choose the path field deliberately, since a field the type does not define is refused, never dropped; (3) extend the hardcoded list in packages/schemas/src/tests/schemas.test.ts:420, which asserts Object.keys(RECORD_TYPES) equals it and that every entry has an fts function, a fileKeys function and a non-empty digest map. The store's FTS and knowledge_create's union follow automatically. To add a queue lane: add it to SYSTEM_REASONS with a DRAIN_VERBS key — a mismatch fails the TypeScript build, and schemas.test.ts:515 re-asserts it at runtime — then write its drain procedure into skills/drain/SKILL.md. Reconcile this article and record-schemas-shared. The checks do NOT catch a fts or fileKeys extractor that reads the wrong field, a new hardcoded type list elsewhere, or a lane with no drain procedure: that last step is manual and unchecked.

## Extensible set: agents — Agents (the roster)

- Registry: agent-templates/registry.json (1:1 with templates)
- Checks: scripts/check-agent-registry.mjs, check-agent-prompts.mjs (§7.3 sections), check-spawn-contracts.mjs (§7.4), check-tool-grants.mjs (real tool names, both MCP prefixes, ToolSearch), check-skills.mjs (skill and command references), check-agents-visible.mjs (runtime)

**Extending this:** To add an agent: (1) write agent-templates/<name>.md with the required prompt sections in order, a valid spawn contract, and a `tools:` line that declares BOTH MCP prefixes for every granted store tool plus ToolSearch; (2) add `{name, file}` to agent-templates/registry.json — no class field; (3) run `npm run check`: a registry/template mismatch, a bad spawn contract, a missing prompt section or an unreal or single-prefix grant each fail their own arm by name; (4) name the agent in the conductor contract's roster and in any skill that routes work to it, or check-skills and the conductor will not know it exists; (5) `node scripts/install-agents.mjs` here, /sterling:sync-agents for siblings, then RESTART — agents load at session start, never live; (6) reconcile this article and agent-distribution. Every dispatch pins its model explicitly. The checks do NOT catch whether the agent behaves correctly once dispatched — that takes a real spawn — nor a stale installed copy in a sibling project, which only H1's agent-currency line reports.

## Extensible set: hooks — Hooks (the knowledge loop at platform seams)

- Registry: hooks/hooks.json (project-level registrations)
- Checks: hooks.json emission check (forward-slash commands) + scripts/tests/hooks-full.test.mjs / enforcement.test.mjs

**Extending this:** The presumption is REMOVE, not add. CLAUDE.md: a new incident 'may add a regression test or a policy record. It may NOT add a new enforcement program (hook, gate, scanner) — the stable unit of growth is policy data', and a mechanism stays only with 'a measured catch no record or test can replace; the burden of proof is on keeping'. The reason is the user's scale-down ruling of 2026-09-19 — 'All the rules and locks is friction, so I want to scale it down ALOT!' — which cut 17 hook families. If a hook is still justified: (1) write the source under scripts/hooks/, taking cwd only from readStdin(); (2) register it in hooks/hooks.json with a forward-slash command; (3) `npm run build:hooks`, confirm check-bundles-fresh, and commit the bundle WITH its source in one commit — otherwise tests pass on the source while the running hook is unchanged (anti_pattern 7cfc5b03); (4) pin it in scripts/tests/ by spawning the bundle; (5) give it an owning family article and reconcile this one; (6) EXIT AND RELAUNCH. The checks do NOT catch a session still running the old bundle: a /clear never reloads hook code.

## Extensible set: tools — Tools (the §10 MCP surface)

- Registry: packages/mcp-server/src/server.ts — registerTool set (the one write path to the store; H15 guards shell bypass)
- Checks: server.test.ts exact tool-list assertion + zod input schemas per tool

**Extending this:** To add a tool: (1) implement it as a SterlingTools method in tools.ts; (2) add one `server.registerTool('<snake_case>', {description, inputSchema: strict zod}, handler)` call in server.ts — unknown parameters must be refused, not dropped; (3) add the name to SERVED_TOOLS in packages/mcp-server/src/tests/server.test.ts:16-45 — the end-to-end test asserts client.listTools() deep-equals it (:316-317), so registered-but-unlisted or listed-but-unregistered fails loudly; (4) grant it in the agent-templates/*.md `tools:` lines that need it, both prefixes, then `node scripts/check-tool-grants.mjs`, which derives the registered names from server.ts itself (readRegisteredToolNames, scripts/lib/checks.mjs:106) and fails on a grant naming an unreal tool or missing a prefix or ToolSearch; (5) add the tool's tests beside its concept and reconcile the sibling article that owns that concept, or create one; (6) rebuild, then EXIT AND RELAUNCH — a /clear keeps the old server. The checks do NOT catch an inputSchema that disagrees with how the handler uses its arguments, nor a description that drifts from behavior.

## Extensible set: toolchain-adapters — Toolchain adapters (per-stack capability layer)

- Registry: scripts/adapters/registry.json — name → module, fixed interface (capabilities/testPathGlobs/runCommands/runTests)
- Checks: checkAdapterRegistry() via scripts/check-agent-registry.mjs + adapter tests in scripts/tests/enforcement.test.mjs

**Extending this:** To add an adapter: (1) write scripts/adapters/<name>.mjs exporting `name`, `capabilities`, `testPathGlobs`, `runCommands` and `runTests({cwd, scope})` — match node.mjs's shape exactly, because the check loads every registered module and validates the interface; (2) add `{name, module}` to scripts/adapters/registry.json; (3) run `npm run check`: checkAdapterRegistry() rides inside scripts/check-agent-registry.mjs (:10, :67) and fails, by adapter name, on an entry with no module file, an unloadable module or a missing export; (4) add interface and routing tests to scripts/tests/enforcement.test.mjs, which already imports the node and pester adapters; (5) give the adapter's behavior an owner — extend git-ro-and-toolchain-adapters's files[] or create an article — and reconcile this one's member list. The check does NOT catch whether runTests() really runs the declared runCommands for a real project, nor whether testPathGlobs are well-formed or overlap another adapter's: those surface only at test-routing time.
